data.name: Frida
data.long_meaning: Frida is derived from the Old Latin word frigidus, meaning 'cold' or 'free.' In the Christian tradition, Frida is a feminine name with a rich history and powerful symbolism, representing peace, purity, and strength. This name was borne by several saints, including St. Frida of Säben and St. Frida of Mecklenburg. It is also associated with the Virgin Mary and the Holy Spirit.

in_hebrew.name: פרידה
in_hebrew.meaning: שם נשים שמקורו בגרמנית, נגזר מ'פריד' שפירושו שלום
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם פרידה הוא שם נשים שמקורו בגרמנית, ונגזר מהמילה 'פריד' שפירושו שלום. הוא קשור למושג השלום והאהבה, ומשמש כסמל לשלווה ואושר. השם פרידה אינו מופיע ישירות בתנ"ך, אך הוא קשור למושגים של שלום ואהבה המופיעים בכתבי הקודש.

in_greek.name: Φρίδα
in_greek.meaning: θηλυκός όνομα γερμανικής προέλευσης, σημαίνει ειρήνη
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Φρίδα είναι γερμανικής προέλευσης και σημαίνει ειρήνη. Είναι ένα σύμβολο ειρήνης και αγάπης, και έχει χρησιμοποιηθεί ως όνομα για κορίτσια στην Ελλάδα και σε άλλες χώρες. Αν και δεν αναφέρεται άμεσα στη Νέα Διαθήκη, η έννοια της ειρήνης είναι κεντρική στο χριστιανικό μήνυμα.

data.cultural_impact: Frida is a name found primarily in Spanish-speaking cultures, with its earliest documented use in the Middle Ages. It has remained a popular name in Mexico and other parts of Latin America, and is particularly beloved in the artistic community due to the legacy of Frida Kahlo, the iconic Mexican painter. Frida Kahlo used her name to evoke a unique blend of tradition, rebellion, and personal identity. Her artistic works, which dealt intimately with her own pain and suffering, continue to captivate audiences around the world.
data.spiritual_significance: From a Christian perspective, the name Frida carries a deep spiritual significance. It is a reminder of the warmth and comfort found within the church community and the peace that comes from living a virtuous life following the teachings of Jesus. Additionally, the name has been associated with St. Frida of Säben, a holy women who lived in the sixth century, and St. Frida of Mecklenburg, who lived in the thirteenth century. Both women were known for their piety, strength, and dedication to the service of God. In this way, the name Frida represents a connection to the divine, echoing the profound spiritual influence of these Christian saints.
